subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Unless necessary to comply with a non-discretionary standard of these regulations,
paragraphs: may not condition approval of an application for residential development or for the housing portion of a mixed-use development to: 1) Require a larger lot size than the minimum required in the applicable zoning district; 2) Require more parking spaces than the minimum required under these regulations; 3) Limit building size to less than allowed in the applicable district including reducing the building footprint or height; 4) Limit the residential density below that allowed in the applicable district; or 5) Otherwise disallow development that abides by the applicable standards of these regulations.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Must specifically describe any conditions or limitations in the written decision. Any
paragraphs: conditions attached to the Development Review Board approval will be considered part Town of Danville Zoning Bylaw - November 28, 2024 of any subsequent zoning permit issued by the Zoning Administrator for the approved development.

sections.title: The Development Review Board may recess a hearing on any application or appeal pending
paragraphs: the submission of additional information, provided that the next hearing date and place is announced at the hearing.

sections.title: Any action or decision of the Development Review Board must be agreed upon by a majority
paragraphs: of the appointed members.

sections.title: In accordance with 24 VSA S4464(b), the Development Review Board shall issue all
paragraphs: decisions within 45 days after the adjournment of the hearing. Failure to issue a decision within the 45-day period shall be deemed approval and shall be effective the 46th day.

sections.title: All decisions shall be issued in writing and shall separately state findings of fact and
paragraphs: conclusions of law. Findings of fact shall explicitly and concisely restate the underlying facts that support the decision, based exclusively on evidence of the record. Conclusions shall be based on the findings of fact. The decision shall also include a statement of the time within which appeals may be taken. The minutes of a meeting may suffice, provided that the factual basis and conclusions relating to the review standards are provided in accordance with these requirements.

sections.title: In rendering a decision in favor of the applicant or appellant, the Development Review
paragraphs: Board may attach additional reasonable conditions and safeguards as it deems necessary to implement these regulations and the Town Plan currently in effect.

sections.title: The Zoning Administrator shell send all decisions by certified mail, within the required 45-
paragraphs: day period, to the applicant or the appellant on matters of appeal. The Zoning Administrator shell also mail copies of the decision to every person appearing who participated at the hearing and file copies of the decision as part of the public record of the Town of Danville.

sections.title: Zoning Permits
Zoning permits and letters of denial shall include a statement of the time within which
paragraphs: appeals may be taken.

sections.title: Permits for uses and subdivisions (not signs) shall require posting of a notice of permit, on a
paragraphs: form prescribed by the Town of Danville. The Zoning Administrator or the applicant shall post this notice of permit within view from the public right-of-way nearest the subject property until the time for appeal has expired. If the Zoning Administrator or applicant does not post the notice of permit within 3 days, the time limit for appeals shall be extended by the length of the delay in posting.

sections.title: The Zoning Administrator, within 3 days of the date of issuance shall:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: request the Road Foreman to review and perform a Site Visit if necessary, and report
paragraphs: back on permit requests that fall within the Town of Danville road right of ways such as curb cuts, fences, hedges, mailboxes, etc.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: post a copy of the permit in the Town of Danville town offices for a period of 15 days
paragraphs: from the date of issuance.

sections.title: No zoning permit shall take effect until the time for appeal has passed, or in the event that a
paragraphs: notice of appeal is properly filed, until final adjudication of the appeal. Town of Danville Zoning Bylaw - November 28, 2024

sections.title: Zoning permits shall remain in effect for two years from the date of issuance. The start of
paragraphs: construction must occur within this two-year period and construction must be complete within five years or reapplication shall be required to continue development.

sections.title: Within 30 days of the issuance of a zoning permit, the Zoning Administrator shall deliver the
paragraphs: original, a legible copy, or a notice of the permit to the Danville Town Clerk for recording in the Town of Danville land records.

sections.title: The Zoning Administrator shall properly file and maintain a record of:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: All permits issued in areas covered by this bylaw,

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Elevation Certificates with the as-built elevation (consistent with the datum of the
paragraphs: elevation on the current Flood Insurance Rate Maps for the community) of the lowest floor, including basement, of all new or substantially improved buildings (not including accessory buildings) in the Special Flood Hazard Area,

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: All flood proofing and other certifications required under this regulation; and,

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: All decisions of the Board (including variances and violations) and all supporting
paragraphs: findings of fact, conclusions, and conditions.

sections.title: Appeals
Interested Persons are defined under 24 VSA S4465 as:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: A person owning title to property, or a municipality or solid waste management district
paragraphs: empowered to condemn it or an interest in it, affected by a bylaw, who alleges that the bylaw imposes on the property unreasonable or inappropriate restrictions of present or potential use under the particular circumstances of the case,

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: The Town of Danville or any adjoining municipality,

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: A person owning or occupying property in the immediate area of a property which is the
paragraphs: subject of a decision or act taken under these regulations, who can demonstrate a physical or environmental impact on the person's interests under the criteria reviewed, and who alleges that the decision or act, if confirmed, will not be in accord with the policies, purposes, or terms of the Town of Danville Town Plan and / or Zoning Bylaw,

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Any combination of at least 20 voters, residents or land owners within the Town of
paragraphs: Danville who, by signed petition to the Development Review Board, allege that any relief requested by a person under this section, if granted, will not be in compliance with the policies, purposes, or terms of the Town of Danville Town Plan and / or Zoning Bylaw, and

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Any department or administrative subdivision of the state owning property or any
paragraphs: interest therein within the municipality, and the Vermont Agency of Commerce and Community Development.

sections.title: Any Interested Person may appeal a decision or act of the Zoning Administrator within 15
paragraphs: days of the date of the decision or act by filing a notice of appeal with the Town Clerk, and by filing a copy of the notice with the Zoning Administrator. A notice of appeal filed under this section shall be in writing and include the following information: Town of Danville Zoning Bylaw - November 28, 2024

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: the name and address of the appellant,

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: a brief description of the property with respect to which the appeal is taken,

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: a reference to applicable provisions of these regulations,

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: the relief requested by the appellant, including any request for a variance from one or
paragraphs: more provisions of these regulations, and

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: the alleged grounds as to why such relief is believed proper under the circumstances
paragraphs: including any new facts or concerns.

sections.title: The Development Review Board shall hold a public hearing on a notice of appeal within 60
paragraphs: days of its filing, as required in 24 VSA S4468. The Development Review Board shall give public notice of the hearing and shall mail a copy of the hearing notice to the appellant not less than 15 days prior to the hearing date.

sections.title: The Development Review Board may reject an appeal or request for reconsideration without
paragraphs: hearing and render a decision which shall include findings of fact within 10 days of the filing of a notice of appeal, if the Development Review Board determines that the issues raised by the appellant have been decided in an earlier appeal or are based on substantially or materially the same facts presented by or on behalf of the appellant.

sections.title: All appeal hearings shall be open to the public and shall be conducted in accordance with
paragraphs: the Development Review Board's rules of procedures, as required by 24 VSA S4461. Any interested person or body may appear and be heard in person or be represented by an agent or attorney at the hearing. The hearing may be adjourned by the Development Review Board from time to time, provided that the date, time, and place of the continuation of the hearing are announced at the hearing.

sections.title: A decision on appeal shall be rendered within 45 days after the final adjournment of the
paragraphs: hearing. The decision shall be sent by certified mail to the appellant within the 45-day period. Copies of the decision shall be mailed to every person or body appearing and having been heard at the hearing and filed with the Zoning Administrator and the Town Clerk as part of the public records of the Town of Danville. If the Development Review Board fails to issue a decision within this 45-day period, the appeal will be deemed approved and shall be effective on the 46th day.

sections.title: Appeals to Environmental Court:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: In accordance with 24 VSA S4471, an interested person who has offered oral or written
paragraphs: testimony in a hearing of the Development Review Board may appeal a decision within 30 days of such decision, to the Vermont Environmental Court.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: The notice of appeal shall be filed by certified mailing, with fees, to the Environmental
paragraphs: Court and by mailing a copy to the Zoning Administrator of the Town of Danville, who shall supply a list of persons who have offered oral or written testimony (including the applicant if not the appellant), to the appellant within 5 working days.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Upon receipt of the list of persons referenced in subsection (b) above, the appellant
paragraphs: shall, by certified mail, provide a copy of the notice of appeal to every person on said list. If any one or more of those persons are not then parties to the appeal, upon motion they shall be granted leave by the court to intervene. Town of Danville Zoning Bylaw - November 28, 2024

sections.title: Certificate of Occupancy
No use of any land or structure may commence until the Zoning Administrator has issued a
paragraphs: Certificate of Occupancy in accordance with 24 VSA S4449. Previous versions of this bylaw called for a Certificate of Compliance which is the same as a Certificate of Occupancy. Note that signs and subdivisions do not require a Certificate of Occupancy.

sections.title: When the Zoning Administrator issues a zoning permit, he or she shall also issue an
paragraphs: application for a Certificate of Occupancy. Prior to the use of the land or structure, the applicant shall submit a completed Certificate of Occupancy application to the Zoning Administrator.

sections.title: When submitting an application for a Certificate of Occupancy, the applicant shall also
paragraphs: submit a copy of the septic permit, certificates as required by 30 VSA S51 (residential building energy standards) or S 53 (commercial building energy standards), and elevation and other floodproofing certificates (or letters determining that such permits are not required) as applicable.

sections.title: The Zoning Administrator shall not issue a Certificate of Occupancy until all necessary
paragraphs: approvals and permits required by these regulations have been obtained for the project and the project has been fully completed in conformance with all such approvals and permits.

sections.title: Within 30 days of receipt of the application for a Certificate of Occupancy, the Zoning
paragraphs: Administrator or their delegate shall inspect the premises to ensure that all work has been completed in conformance with the zoning permit and associated approvals, including all applicable permit conditions. If the Zoning Administrator fails to either grant or deny the Certificate of Occupancy within 30 days of the submission of an application, the Certificate of Occupancy shall be deemed issued on the 31st day.

sections.title: If an applicant does not submit an application for a Certificate of Occupancy within 30 days
paragraphs: of completing a project, the applicant is in violation of this bylaw, and after suitable reminders and warnings may be subject to penalties in accordance with this bylaw. Town of Danville Zoning Bylaw - November 28, 2024

sections.title: Overview
Signs are regulated to promote and protect public safety, encourage use of signs as a means
paragraphs: of effective communication, protect the economic and scenic value of the Town, and ensure a fair and consistent simple process for permitting of signs and clear enforcement of the bylaw.

sections.title: No sign, whether temporary or permanent, shall be erected, installed, or altered unless in
paragraphs: conformance with all applicable provisions of this bylaw. Signs do not require a permit unless the express terms of this bylaw state that a permit is required. If a permit is required, no sign shall be erected, installed, or altered until a permit has been issued for such sign by the Zoning Administrator or Development Review Board as applicable.

sections.title: If signage is part of a larger proposed development, the signage review process can be
paragraphs: integrated with the normal review process.

sections.title: Signs That Do Not Require a Permit
Signs identified below are authorized in all districts and do not require a sign permit when
paragraphs: located on the parcel upon which the advertised is located, or when located on another parcel with the permission of the owner:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Signs erected, maintained, or administered by the Town or the State of Vermont under
paragraphs: Title 10, VSA, Chapter 21.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Unlighted signs not exceeding 2 square feet in area (per side excluding frame and
paragraphs: mounting hardware) or smaller including those bearing property names, numbers, post box numbers or names of occupants of premises.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Legal notices and identification, informational, warning, or directional signs displayed
paragraphs: in response to government regulations or requirements or informational signs on government buildings that identify the building.

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Temporary signs advertising the sale of property on which the sign is located, not
paragraphs: exceeding 6 square feet in area (per side excluding frame and mounting hardware). Signs must be removed with completion of sale.

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Small signs without advertising displayed for the direction, instruction, or convenience
paragraphs: of the public, including signs which identify rest rooms, posted areas, parking lots or the like with an area not exceeding 2 square feet in area (per side excluding frame and mounting hardware), provided the signs are on the premises of the activity served by the sign.

subsections.label: F
subsections.title: One "Open" or "Welcome" banner or flag per parcel or lot, provided that such sign has
paragraphs: no other wording or logos, is less than 15 square feet in area (per side excluding mounting hardware) and is used in conjunction with a permitted non-residential use.

subsections.label: G
subsections.title: Temporary signs to be maintained for not more than 2 weeks erected by fairs,
paragraphs: expositions, non-profit organizations, or signs announcing a garage sale, yard sale or auction, or an event of a civic, political, philanthropic service, or religious organization, not exceeding 10 square feet in area. These signs may be located off-premises with the Town of Danville Zoning Bylaw - November 28, 2024 permission of the landowner. All such signs must be removed by the owner within 24 hours following the event or they may be removed by the Town at the sign owner's expense.

subsections.label: H
subsections.title: Temporary agricultural based signs advertising the sale of seasonal produce or
paragraphs: products not exceeding 10 square feet in area.

subsections.label: I
subsections.title: Signs for a maximum of two registered and inspected motor vehicles offered for private
paragraphs: sale, except when such vehicles are being used primarily for advertising.

subsections.label: J
subsections.title: State or National flags

subsections.label: K
subsections.title: Temporary contractor signs not exceeding 6 square feet in area (per side excluding
paragraphs: frame and mounting hardware) located on the property where the work is being performed and to be removed upon completion of work.

subsections.label: L
subsections.title: Political signage following established State of Vermont regulations

subsections.label: M
subsections.title: Temporary sign not exceeding 32 square feet in area which provides information to the
paragraphs: public regarding construction projects. The sign shall be located on the property where the work is being performed and shall be removed upon completion of work.

sections.title: Signs That Require a Permit
The following standards will apply to all signs that require a permit:

subsections.label: A
subsections.title: Signs shall be located on the parcel or lot where the advertised business, product or
paragraphs: activity is located or sold.

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Signs shall not prevent a clear and unobstructed view of official signs or other permitted
paragraphs: signs or otherwise impede adequate sight distance.

subsections.label: C
subsections.title: Signs shall not appear to direct the movement of traffic or interfere with, imitate, or
paragraphs: resemble any official traffic, directional or route sign, signal, or device.

subsections.label: D
subsections.title: Signs shall not contain any animated, flashing, fluttering, revolving, or moving parts nor
paragraphs: any fluorescent paint or coloring, neon, or electronic LED messaging.

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Signs shall not be within or over the right-of-way to public roads except for signs in the
paragraphs: Village Core district and temporary public service announcements approved by the DRB.

subsections.label: F
subsections.title: Signs shall not be erected, attached, or maintained upon trees or drawn or painted on
paragraphs: rocks or other natural features or upon utility poles.

subsections.label: G
subsections.title: Signs and other advertising structures, together with all their supports, braces, hooks,
paragraphs: guys, and anchors shall be substantial and sturdy construction, shall be kept in good repair, and shall be painted or cleaned as often as necessary to maintain clean, neat, safe and orderly appearance.

subsections.label: H
subsections.title: No sign shall incorporate a public address system or other audio system

subsections.label: I
subsections.title: Lighting of signs shall be shielded to prevent glare off-site, into the sky, or onto adjoining
paragraphs: properties or roads. Town of Danville Zoning Bylaw - November 28, 2024

subsections.label: J
subsections.title: Total signage per non-residential / business shall not exceed 64 square feet where
paragraphs: permitted.

subsections.label: K
subsections.title: Free standing or signs attached to buildings or structures shall not exceed 20 feet in
paragraphs: height from grade.

subsections.label: L
subsections.title: Portable signs (mounted on wheels, trailers, or motor vehicles if those vehicles or
paragraphs: wheeled signs are regularly located for fixed display) are not permitted.
